title: Cross-Task Activation Probe Transfer: Do Deception Probes Trained on One Domain Generalize to Another?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Addresses a critical open problem: labs cannot train probes for every domain. A cross-domain transfer matrix directly informs scalability of activation monitoring. Clear link from finding to deployment strategy.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training deception probes on activation data is established methodology. However, setting up three distinct task domains (factual QA, code generation, tool use) and creating prompted-deception datasets for each adds complexity. Medium compute suffices.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Core experiment is clear (train probe on domain A, test on B), but doing it across three domains with a transfer matrix and mixture experiments stretches scope. Could be narrowed to two domains to fit 30 hours.
